name: Glio-Oubi
catalog_citation: Jaffe, Jenny & Sebastian Nordhoff. 2021. The documentation of the Kru language Oubi. Handout (13 pp.) and presentation slides, Africanist Colloquium, Humboldt-Universitat zu Berlin, 2021-06-08. Zenodo working paper, doi:10.5281/zenodo.4910759 (CC-BY 4.0).
catalog_locator: Handout section 4.3 'Tones', p. 5 (with Fig. 5 pitch tracks p. 5-6 and Fig. 6 'fourfold minimal pair nyoro', p. 6; also 5.1 p. 8 'we have no insights into the tone system' and 6.1 p. 11 'Past/perfective is not segmentally marked. A marking via tones is probable.'); presentation slide 'Tones'.
catalog_quote: 4.3 Tones. There are at least three different tones. See Figures 5 and 6. Given the linguistic (Dutch, American) and professional (vet) background of Jaffe, an analysis or even a transcription of the tone system was beyond the possibilities of this project. It is hoped that this shortcoming will soon be fixed by researchers with more training in this area. [slides, 'Tones'] There are at least three tones, possibly more. Analysis of the tonal system is beyond our capacities. No attempt is made to indicate tones on the examples given here. below: 'my father' and 'your father', both segmentally nambi, but with different tones.

new_statements.relation_note: 7 vowels, 25 consonants (prenasalised mb nd, gb; possible pw gw hw), vowel length unresolved, syllable (C)(L)V(:)(N), at least three tones with Praat pitch figures, possible vowel harmony; no stress/accent statement.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Oubi (Tai variety) is tonal with at least three contrastive tones (possibly more), shown by tonal minimal pairs (nambi 'my father' vs 'your father'; nyoro 'woman/women/day/name'); the tone system is not analysed and tones are not transcribed; nothing is said about word stress or accent.
new_statements.exceptions: none; authors state the number of tones is a lower bound and that vowel quality may also distinguish the nyoro set
new_statements.identity_note: Explicitly 'Oubi (also called Glio).. Western Kru.. spoken in Cote d'Ivoire.. The variety represented here is from the Tai national park'; repository named glio1241; speakers recorded at the Tai chimpanzee research station; ISO/glottocode match (oub/glio1241). | 'Language: Oubi (ISO639-3:oub)', 'Location: Cote d'Ivoire', 'mainly carried out in Tai National Park, at the Tai Chimpanzee Project amongst its Oubi staff'; contrasts these speakers with 'the Oubi speakers over the border in Libera' = Glio-Oubi glio1241, Tai (Ivorian) variety, same speakers as work 1.

new_statements.quote: 1 recording of words that only differ in tonality [...] Orthographic convention: The Oubi orthography used in the transcriptions is not fully consistent, mainly using French orthography with some Dutch influences. The nasalised n at the end of syllabes (similar to as in the French word 'pain') is written with a capital N. [...] As the written orthography gives no information at all about tonality, which can be crucial for word meaning, the recordings particularly important. [French parallel: 1 enregistrement de mots qui ne different que par leur tonalite ... Comme l'orthographe ecrite ne donne aucune information sur la tonalite, qui peut etre cruciale pour la signification des mots, les enregistrements sont particulierement importants.] [bundle oubi_027 description:] Notes on grammar. Description of words for family members, word order (ie SVO), negation, minimal pairs bingo (ie words that only differ in one vowel or consonant), tonality, pluralisation (quite a few different ways of forming plural).
new_statements.citation: Jaffe, Jenny. 2021. Documentation of Oubi. London: Endangered Languages Archive, collection 0653 (dk0653). hdl:2196/00-0000-0000-0003-B45G-H. Open landing-page metadata (summary, contents, 'Other information') plus bundle oubi_027 'Grammar, pluralisation, minimal pairs' (Notes, created 2019-12-01, file, hdl:2196/9bc466ed-304c-4023-95a5-5c85218ad6d0, access U) -- same deposit as A's work 3, re-reported because its open description page could be read and does say something about tone.
new_statements.locator: ELAR dk0653 landing page, sections 'Collection contents' (bullet 5) and 'Other Information: Orthographic convention'; bundle page oubi_027 'Grammar, pluralisation, minimal pairs', Description and Keywords (Tonality, Pronunciation, Minimal pairs).
new_statements.relation_note: Tone is meaning-distinguishing and unmarked in the ad hoc French-based orthography (final nasal written N); one recorded session of tone-only minimal pairs; grammar-notes PDF covers pronunciation, minimal pairs and tonality (not opened: registered-user access). No stress/accent wording on the landing page, browse page, bundle page or the 2021 ELAR blog post (blog only: 'the tonalities were a skill I never mastered').
new_statements.rule_in_words: Depositor's metadata states that tone ('tonality') distinguishes word meanings in Oubi (a session of words differing only in tone was recorded) and that the practical orthography does not mark it; nothing on stress or accent. Corroborates work 1 (at least three lexical tones) from the same project; no analysis of the system.

sources.citation: Nordhoff, Sebastian & Jenny Jaffe. 2019-2021. glio1241: A description of the Oubi language (online grammar-in-progress: phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, wordlist, audio). GitHub Pages, repository lgdesc/glio1241 (last pushed 2021-06-07).
sources.note: Phonology index lists 'tonology' as a covered topic but the Tonology page is empty; PhonologicalInventory gives vowel and consonant charts with example words, SyllableStructure gives (C)(L)V(:)(N) with syllabic nasal m 'five'; VowelHarmony a stub. No tone or stress statement on the site itself (the statement is in the 2021 handout, work 1).
